audit.why: packet.levelChart is Skill on rows 0-5 and Vladimir on row 6; full phases[].side and content win[] match it exactly, and the 45.48% winRate over 1117 games is consistent with an even lane that loses late. No flips needed.

audit.whatIsWrong: The spike prose describes the right windows but names no numbers, so 'bait the Pool' has no size attached. Sanguine Pool is 28/25/22/19/16s and Vladimir almost never maxes it, so the punish window in lane is roughly 25-28 seconds. Transfusion falls to 4.6s at max rank.
audit.why: Concrete cooldowns are what make the bait-then-commit rule actionable; the page's own approved bar demands real numbers where they make advice concrete.
audit.corrected: Pool's 2-second untargetability and its 25-28s lane cooldown added to spikes[1] and early; Transfusion's 4.6s added to spikes[2].
sources: enemyKit W cd 28/25/22/19/16 and text '2 seconds'

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2].text credits Vladimir's HP recovery to 'Crimson Rush', which is not an ability. His passive is Crimson Pact — a stat conversion (30 bonus health per 1 AP, 1 AP per 1.6 bonus health), not a heal. The sustain comes from Transfusion and Hemoplague, not from the passive.
audit.why: packet.defects flagged this and the kit confirms it. The invented name also misinforms about the mechanic: telling a player his passive heals him leads them to build anti-heal expecting it to blunt the passive, which it does not.
audit.corrected: Crimson Rush -> Crimson Pact, described correctly as the health/AP conversion; the healing attributed to Transfusion where it belongs.

audit.why: Grievous Wounds is genuinely load-bearing here: Transfusion, Sanguine Pool's siphon and Hemoplague all carry heal flags. report[8].t and wants.you[1] already prescribe early anti-heal.

edits.before: Still close after first item, though the tide starts turning; his Transfusion (Q) heal and Crimson Rush let him claw back the HP your burst removes if you can't chain the kill instantly.
edits.after: Still close after first item, though the tide turns; Transfusion (Q) heals every 4.6s at max rank and Crimson Pact turns his health items into AP, so he claws back the HP your burst removes.

edits.before: Roughly even at 6: your Purgatory (R) can execute him, but his Pool (W) is an untargetable dodge that eats the totem's window, so it becomes a mind-game over baiting the Pool before you commit.
edits.after: Roughly even at 6: Purgatory (R) can execute him, but Pool (W) is 2 seconds of untargetability that eats the totem's window — bait it first, and with W left unmaxed you get a 25-28s gap to kill him in.

edits.before: Early is a genuine skill matchup decided by who respects cooldowns. Your Q-nail poke and W spike can punish Vladimir's flimsy early base stats, but his Sanguine Pool erases any all-in you mistime, so bait it out before you E in. Trade when his Transfusion is on cooldown and his Pool is down. Don't let your W self-damage leave you low into his Q harass while he's healthy.
edits.after: Early is a genuine skill matchup decided by who respects cooldowns. Your Q-nail poke and W spike can punish Vladimir's flimsy early base stats, but Sanguine Pool erases any mistimed all-in — it is 28 seconds at rank 1, so bait it and the lane is yours for half a minute. Don't let your W self-damage leave you low into his Q harass while he's healthy.

notes: packet defect confirmed real: 'Crimson Rush' does not exist — Vladimir's passive is Crimson Pact and it is a stat conversion, not sustain. Chart already agrees across both layers and the packet; nothing flipped, so no mirror conflict with vladimir__locke.
